answer: Model agents as a trust graph seeded by a few long-audited, bonded nodes that act as an anchor. Reputation flows out from each anchor, but a vertex can pass on only as much trust as its incoming edges carry, capped per epoch. An attacker can mint a thousand fake vertices for free, yet all of them hang off the few edges won from honest agents, so the swarm splits that thin trickle. Like a sparrow flock, it is loud and numerous but weighs little. Gaining real influence means earning each honest vouch, and every voucher stakes a bond that is slashed if its fakes are caught.
